source.title: Exact Unlearning of Finetuning Data via Model Merging at Scale
source.authors: Kevin Kuo; Amrith Rajagopal Setlur; K. Srinivas; Aditi Raghunathan; Virginia Smith

page_placements.theme: Membership-inference residue after unlearning (privacy signal, under- or over-unlearning)

record.tranche_reason: Uses approximate unlearning methods as baselines and cites attack brittleness as motivation, but does not test whether recovery attacks succeed after unlearning.
record.gate_note: The MUSE-News table reports forgetting, memorization, privacy-leakage, and retain-utility metrics for approximate and exact unlearning methods. These are unlearning outcomes, not tests of recovery by fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, or prompting. The paper's other merging and unlearning results do not evaluate those attacks.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes SIFT-Masks, an exact-unlearning method built on merging, and cites prior attack results only as motivation. It runs no attack after unlearning: no relearning, activation ablation, quantization or prompting. The MUSE-News appendix reports forgetting, PrivLeak and retain metrics for GA/NPO baselines. PrivLeak is a membership-inference score, not a recovery-attack result. Nothing bears on whether any version holds. The baselines are comparators for the authors' own method, not a use of the finding as a tool, so T6 fits better than T4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate for the MUSE-News appendix but misses the main conclusion. The main conclusion is that SIFT-Masks (sign-fixed tuning plus local masks) makes merging-based exact unlearning efficient at scale. It improves accuracy 5-80% over naive merging and uses up to 250x less unlearning compute than other merging baselines.
record.recipe_differences: SIFT-Masks uses deterministic task-level fine-tuning, model merging, and local masks to enable exact unlearning of fine-tuning data; it is not an attack or a reproduction of gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model/task settings affect merging accuracy and unlearning costs; the MUSE-News table is one evaluation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: On MUSE-News with Llama2-7b, GA GDR and NPO GDR cut VerbMem (58.4 to 4.9 and 1.2) but have PrivLeak of 108.1 and 105.8. Their Retain utility also drops, from 55.2 to 27.3 and 40.5. The exact merging methods have PrivLeak 0, and SIFT-Masks has Retain 48.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On MUSE-News, approximate unlearning (GA/NPO) lowers memorization but leaves membership-inference leakage and costs retain utility. Exact merging-based unlearning has zero PrivLeak.

record.peer_reviewed: 2026 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
record.problems: The MUSE-News evidence is reported for one model and one dataset; no uncertainty estimates are given. PrivLeak is a membership-inference metric, not a test of the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted; the rows record the separately reported MUSE-News metrics. Other experiments concern merging accuracy, storage, or unlearning compute rather than post-unlearning recovery.

untested.parts: No attack after unlearning, and no targeted-knowledge accuracy measured against chance. GA/NPO baselines are reported only on MUSE-News forget and retain metrics.
No activation ablation and no analysis of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
SIFT-Masks is exact by construction (unmerging the task vector), but its resistance to the listed attacks is never tested empirically.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's concern is exact unlearning of fine-tuning data through task-vector subtraction. Brittleness of approximate unlearning (refs 10-12) is cited only in the introduction and related work. The MUSE-News evaluation is a single appendix table, from one run with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test simple attacks after unlearning or report targeted-knowledge accuracy relative to chance for this claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether targeted knowledge is stored but inaccessible.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery attack.
SIFT-Masks is presented as an exact unlearning method, but the paper does not test its resistance to the listed attacks.

relation.reason: The abstract and related work cite prior attacks on approximate unlearning only as motivation.

tranche.reason: The paper proposes an exact-unlearning method (SIFT-Masks, merging plus masks). It runs no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting attack on any model, and it does not use the finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: Table XIII has lost its layout, but the values map by order: 7 methods (Target, Retrain, GA GDR, NPO GDR, FT+Merge, TALL-masks, SIFT-Masks) by 4 metrics. Retrain row: VerbMem 20.8, Forget 33.1, PrivLeak 0, Retain 55.0, so GA/NPO push VerbMem below retrain. PrivLeak rows give no baseline (Target -99.8 is in R15; 0 is ideal). R21 and R28 compare the paper's own method with baselines. The only Llama prompt in the text is an example sentiment template.
